## 0. Glossary (MANDATORY, read first)

Terms are defined once here and used consistently in every FR below. Nouns that could drive two
different code paths are flagged so implementers do not conflate them.

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Island** | The new notification presentation: a pure-black capsule anchored top-center that spring-morphs between a compact pill and an expanded card. One of two presentations; the other is the existing top-right glass **card**. |
| **Card (top-right)** | The EXISTING presentation: a liquid-glass toast stacked at top-right by `NotificationOverlay.tsx`. Not removed by this feature. |
| **Presentation** (FLAGGED: drives two code paths) | The per-notification selector that routes a notification to either the island window or the top-right card window. This is the new routing dimension. It is NOT the same as `style` (visual overrides) and NOT the same as `priority`. Provisional payload field name `presentation: "island" \| "card"` (final name is an Open Question, see OQ-1). |
| **Kind** (FLAGGED: potential alias for presentation) | Used loosely in the brief as a synonym for "presentation". This PRD treats **presentation** as the single canonical noun and RETIRES "kind" to avoid a second code path with the same meaning. Implementers must not introduce a separate `kind` field. |
| **Compact** | The idle / live-activity state of the island: a small pill. Shows a leading glyph and a trailing live activity (timer, ring, pulse, or grouped count badge). |
| **Expanded** | The card state of the island: shows icon, sender, title, body, progress, actions, countdown. Same content anatomy as the top-right card, rendered inside the island shape. |
| **Morph** | The single spring-driven transition between compact and expanded. The OS window frame is held at the expanded size; only the SVG shape and inner content animate (D3). |
| **Spotlight** | In Model B overflow (D5), the single highest-priority notification shown in the compact pill when multiple are queued. The rest are represented by an xN count badge. |
| **Live activity** | The trailing compact-state content that conveys ongoing status: a running timer, a progress ring, a pulse dot, or a grouped count. Named after the iOS Dynamic Island concept. |
| **Wall inset** (`--di-wall`) | The horizontal distance from the island's outer edge to where the concave shoulder shape allows content. Content padding is `max(base, wall + margin)` so text never collides with the curved shoulders. A content-vs-shape invariant, not a box-vs-box one. |
| **Capture exclusion** | The OS-level property that keeps the island window out of screen recordings and screen shares. Maps to macOS `NSWindowSharingNone` and Windows `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE` via Tauri `set_content_protected(true)`. No reliable Linux equivalent. |
| **Notch mode** | Island rendering that hugs the physical MacBook notch: top corners square, capsule fused to the notch, compact pill stays pure black even in light appearance. |
| **Float mode** | Island rendering as a fully-rounded floating capsule (non-notch Macs, Windows, Linux). Position is user-selectable (top-left / top-center / top-right / bottom-center). |
| **Persistent settings** (FLAGGED vs payload overrides) | The 13 app-wide island configuration values (geometry, opacity, radii, accent, mode, position, appearance, reduced-motion, capture toggle). Set once in app settings, apply to ALL island notifications. Senders CANNOT set these. Schema = the mockup's `island.settings.json`. |
| **Payload overrides** (FLAGGED vs persistent settings) | The existing 27 per-notification `style` keys (`StyleOverrides` in `src/types/notification.ts`) that map to `--s-*` CSS variables. A sender MAY set these per notification. They control skin/color/typography only, NEVER geometry or position. |

**The load-bearing split (repeated because it drives the whole design):** persistent settings own
GEOMETRY and POSITION and are app-wide; payload overrides own SKIN and are per-notification. Senders
never control where the island is or how big it is.

---

## 1. Introduction / Overview

syncfu is "the notification layer your AI agents are missing." Today it shows one presentation: a
liquid-glass toast pinned top-right. This feature adds a second, additive presentation, the **Dynamic
Island**: a pure-black notch-anchored capsule that spring-morphs between a compact idle pill and an
expanded notification card.

The island fits agent and long-task status (timers, progress, approvals, live activity) better than a
corner toast because it is the most glanceable ambient-status form factor on modern laptops, and it is
**invisible during screen sharing and screen recording**, which lets developers stream, pair, and demo
while agents run without leaking private notifications or secrets on a live capture. Screen-share
invisibility is the category differentiator (the closed-source reference product Notchie markets exactly
this).

The island is **selectable per notification** and coexists with the top-right card; it does not replace
it. All existing behavior (actions, `--wait`, timeouts, progress, grouping, the 27 style overrides) works
in island mode.

---

## 2. Users

| User | Context | What they need from the island |
|------|---------|-------------------------------|
| **Agent author** (integrator) | Writes code or an MCP tool that calls `syncfu send` / HTTP / WS to surface agent status. | A one-field way to route a notification to the island, without having to reason about geometry or positioning. |
| **Developer approving decisions** | Runs long agent tasks; must approve or reject `--wait` decisions (exit codes 0/1/2). | The island expands and stays expanded on a decision, offers primary/secondary/danger actions, blocks the CLI until answered, and does not steal focus. |
| **Streamer / presenter** | Streams, pairs, or demos while agents run. Private notifications and secrets must not appear on the recording. | The island is excluded from OS screen capture by default, verifiably, on macOS and Windows; a documented, predictable behavior on Linux. |
| **Customizing user** | Wants the island to match their screen, brand, or taste, once, for all island notifications. | A persistent settings surface (geometry, opacity, radii, accent, mode, position, appearance, motion, capture toggle) that applies app-wide and survives restart. |

---

## 3. Goals

- Ship an additive island presentation that reaches functional parity with the top-right card
  (actions, `--wait`, priority timeouts, progress, grouping, all 27 style overrides).
- Reproduce the approved mockup's visual fidelity: shape, spring motion, wall-aware content, and Model B
  overflow, ported from the mockup's reference JS rather than redesigned.
- Guarantee capture exclusion on macOS and Windows, verified on its own dedicated track (D1); ship a
  documented, predictable Linux behavior.
- Give the user one persistent settings surface for the 13 island settings; keep sender payloads limited
  to the existing 27 style overrides.
- Introduce zero regression to the top-right card, the HTTP/WS API, CLI flag compatibility, and history.

---

## 4. User Stories

### US-001: Agent author sends an island notification
**Progress:** To do

**Description:** As an agent author, I want to select the island presentation with a single payload
field and CLI flag so that agent status appears in the notch capsule without me controlling any geometry.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A new per-notification field routes a notification to the island (provisional `presentation: "island"`; default keeps the existing top-right card so current integrations are unchanged).
- [ ] `syncfu send` exposes an equivalent flag (provisional `--presentation island`).
- [ ] The field is accepted over HTTP `:9868` and WS `:9869` with the same schema; an omitted or unknown value falls back to the card presentation and does not error the request.
- [ ] The payload cannot set geometry, position, mode, or opacity; only the existing 27 `style` overrides are honored.
- [ ] Existing payloads with no presentation field behave exactly as today (regression check).
- [ ] Typecheck / lint / `cargo check` pass across the three type files (`cli/src/types.rs`, `src-tauri/src/notification/types.rs`, `src/types/notification.ts`).

### US-002: Developer approves a --wait decision from the island
**Progress:** To do

**Description:** As a developer running a long agent task, I want the island to expand for a decision and
block my CLI until I answer so that I can approve or reject from the glanceable capsule.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A decision notification arrives expanded (or auto-expands) and stays expanded until answered; auto-dismiss is paused while a decision or an open list is showing.
- [ ] Primary, secondary, and danger actions render inside the island shape and are clickable without the window stealing focus from the foreground app.
- [ ] `--wait` blocks the CLI and returns exit code 0 (primary/action), 1 (dismiss), or 2 (timeout), identical to card behavior; critical priority never auto-dismisses.
- [ ] When the island is idle (no decision, no hover), the overlay is click-through.
- [ ] Verify in browser using MCP Playwright tools (expanded decision state + action click).

### US-003: Streamer relies on capture invisibility
**Progress:** To do

**Description:** As a streamer, I want the island hidden from screen recording and sharing by default so
that private notifications never leak on a live capture.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] On macOS the island window is excluded from capture by default; verified by recording the screen and confirming the island is absent (dedicated verification track, D1).
- [ ] On Windows the island window is excluded from capture by default; verified the same way.
- [ ] Capture exclusion works on the actual island window type (NSPanel via `tauri-nspanel` on macOS); if `set_content_protected(true)` does not apply to that window type, an alternate path sets `sharingType = .none` (early gate, see OQ-4).
- [ ] The user can toggle `hideFromScreenCapture` in persistent settings; default is ON.
- [ ] On Linux, the documented behavior (from OQ-5) is implemented and surfaced to the user; the island never silently claims invisibility it cannot deliver.
- [ ] Verify in browser using MCP Playwright tools (island renders); capture-absence verified per-OS outside jsdom.

### US-004: User customizes persistent island settings
**Progress:** To do

**Description:** As a user, I want a settings surface for the island's geometry, appearance, and behavior
so that all my island notifications match my preference and survive an app restart.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Settings expose all 13 persistent keys from `island.settings.json`: `compactWidth`, `expandedWidth`, `height`, `surfaceOpacity`, `topRadius`, `bottomRadius`, `cornerScaling`, `accent`, `mode`, `position`, `appearance`, `reducedMotion`, `hideFromScreenCapture`.
- [ ] Each numeric setting enforces its range and default (see FR-8); out-of-range input is clamped, not accepted raw.
- [ ] Settings persist across app restart.
- [ ] Changing a setting updates the island geometry/appearance without animating the OS window frame (D3 constraint) and without requiring a notification resend.
- [ ] `position` bottom-center is float-mode only and expands upward with the notch shape mirrored vertically; notch-mode compact pill stays black even when `appearance` is light.
- [ ] Verify in browser using MCP Playwright tools (each setting changes the rendered island).

## 5. Functional Requirements

Requirements are grouped and cross-referenced to the locked decisions. Each has acceptance criteria.

### Presentation routing (additive kind)

**FR-1** The system MUST add a per-notification presentation selector that routes a notification to the
island or the top-right card. Provisional field `presentation: "island" | "card"`, default `"card"`.
The field is mirrored across the three type files following the existing enum pattern, exposed as a
`syncfu send` flag, and accepted over HTTP and WS unchanged in transport.
- Acceptance: default-omitted payloads render as top-right cards (regression); `presentation: "island"`
  renders in the island window; unknown values fall back to card without erroring.

**FR-2** Senders MUST NOT be able to control island geometry, position, mode, size, or opacity through
the payload. The payload's only styling surface is the existing 27 `style` overrides (`StyleOverrides`).
- Acceptance: a payload attempting geometry keys is rejected or ignored for those keys; the 27 `style`
  keys still apply and map to `--s-*` variables inside the island.

**FR-3** Island and top-right card presentations MUST coexist. Coexistence routing (can both be on screen
at once, or is one active at a time) is specified in OQ-9 and MUST be resolved before US-001 ships.
- Acceptance: sending an island notification does not close or disturb existing top-right cards, per the
  coexistence rule chosen in OQ-9.

### Anchoring and shape (D3)

**FR-4** In notch mode the island MUST anchor top-center hugging the physical notch: top corners square,
capsule fused to the notch. In float mode it MUST render a fully-rounded capsule pinned to the selected
position.
- Acceptance: on a notched Mac the island top edge is flush with the notch; on non-notch displays and
  Windows/Linux it renders as a floating rounded capsule at the configured position.

**FR-5** The island shape MUST be an SVG path with quadratic-Bezier concave shoulders (control point at
the outer top corner), radii 6/14 compact growing to 19/24 expanded, with clamps
`t <= min(W/4, H/4)` and `b <= min(W/4, H/2)`. This shape generator is PORTED from the mockup's
`notchPath()`, not redesigned.
- Acceptance: rendered corner radii and shoulder curvature match the mockup at compact and expanded
  states within visual-regression tolerance.

**FR-6** The morph MUST animate the SVG shape and inner content only; the OS window frame MUST be held at
the expanded size and never animated (D3, prevents jank documented by all three native reference apps).
Springs: container 220/25, content 400/30, pop 260/18; reduced-motion 1000/100; hover scale 1.028
top-anchored with a 150ms open delay. Spring integrator is PORTED from the mockup, not redesigned.
- Acceptance: the window frame does not resize during morph; springs match the mockup constants;
  reduced-motion preference swaps to the 1000/100 config.

**FR-7** Content inside the island MUST honor the wall-inset rule: content horizontal padding is
`max(base, wall + margin)` using the live `--di-wall` value so text never collides with the concave
shoulders. This is a content-vs-shape invariant.
- Acceptance: at every geometry setting, no title/body/action glyph overlaps the curved shoulder region
  (verified content-vs-shape, not box-vs-box).

### Customization: persistent settings (D4)

**FR-8** The system MUST provide a persistent app-settings surface with these 13 keys, ranges, and
defaults (schema = mockup `island.settings.json`):

| Key | Range | Default | Notes |
|-----|-------|---------|-------|
| `compactWidth` | 150-600 | 218 | pill width |
| `expandedWidth` | 320-560 | 380 | card width |
| `height` | 24-60 | 34 | capsule height |
| `surfaceOpacity` | 0-100% | 94 | surface fill alpha only |
| `topRadius` | (radius range) | per mockup | with `cornerScaling` |
| `bottomRadius` | (radius range) | per mockup | with `cornerScaling` |
| `cornerScaling` | bool | true | scale radii between states |
| `accent` | preset or custom hex | `#4a9eff` | presets + custom |
| `mode` | notch \| float | notch | |
| `position` | left \| center \| right \| bottom-center | center | float mode only; bottom-center expands upward |
| `appearance` | dark \| light \| auto | (per mockup) | notch compact pill stays black in light |
| `reducedMotion` | bool | false | swaps to 1000/100 springs |
| `hideFromScreenCapture` | bool | true | capture exclusion toggle |

- Acceptance: each numeric key clamps to its range; settings survive restart; `position` values other
  than bottom-center are ignored in notch mode; `bottom-center` is rejected in notch mode.

**FR-9** These 13 settings are app-wide and MUST NOT be settable per notification. Payloads that attempt
them MUST have no effect on geometry.
- Acceptance: same payload rendered before and after changing a setting reflects the setting, not the
  payload.

**FR-10** In light appearance, the expanded card and float-mode pills MUST restyle (light frosted
surface, dark text); in macOS notch mode the compact pill MUST stay pure black to blend with the physical
notch.
- Acceptance: light appearance changes expanded surface and float pills; notch compact pill is black in
  both light and dark appearance.

### Overflow: Model B only (D5)

**FR-11** When multiple notifications are queued, the compact island MUST show the highest-priority
**spotlight** item plus an xN count badge. Badge width is `26 + 8 * (digits - 1)` and caps at "9+".
- Acceptance: with N queued, compact shows one spotlight plus a correctly-sized badge; N above 9 shows
  "9+".

**FR-12** Expanding MUST reveal a priority-ranked, deduped list capped at 6 rows / 560px, then scroll
inside the island with a bottom-fade affordance; rows stagger in 40-60ms; critical ranks first;
auto-dismiss is paused while the list is open. Dedupe-key semantics and row-to-action mapping are
specified in OQ-6.
- Acceptance: list is ranked critical-first, deduped, capped at 6 rows before scrolling with a bottom
  fade; auto-dismiss does not fire while the list is open.

**FR-13** Overflow Models A (badge + cycle) and C (stack-under) MUST NOT be implemented. The build MUST
carry an explicit guard so they are not reintroduced without re-adjudication (C is the named
anti-pattern no mature app ships).
- Acceptance: only Model B exists in code; a comment/guard/test names A and C as rejected.

### Functional parity and lifecycle

**FR-14** Island mode MUST reuse existing behavior: actions (primary/secondary/danger), `--wait`
blocking with exit codes 0/1/2, priority timeouts (low 6s / normal 8s / high 12s / critical never),
progress updates (bar and ring), grouping/stacking (via Model B), and all 27 style overrides.
- Acceptance: a matrix of these behaviors passes in island mode identically to card mode.

**FR-15** The system MUST define a compact-vs-expanded lifecycle: when the island arrives expanded vs as
a pill, what triggers expansion (activity / hover / click), what triggers collapse, and how `--wait`
holds it expanded. The exact model is specified in OQ-2 and MUST be resolved before US-002 ships.
- Acceptance: every state transition (arrive, expand, collapse, decision-hold, timeout, dismiss,
  overflow-open) is enumerated with its trigger and its interruption/resume behavior.

**FR-16** The overlay MUST stay click-through when the island is idle and become interactive only when
expanded content requires it (actions, list). Idle morph and hover MUST NOT jank.
- Acceptance: idle island passes clicks to the app beneath; expanded actions receive clicks; morph holds
  60fps target on reference hardware.

### Capture exclusion (D1, dedicated track)

**FR-17** The island window MUST be excluded from OS screen capture by default on macOS
(`NSWindowSharingNone`) and Windows (`WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`) via Tauri `set_content_protected(true)`,
applied to the actual island window type. If the property does not apply to the `tauri-nspanel` NSPanel,
an alternate AppKit path MUST set `sharingType = .none` (OQ-4, early gate).
- Acceptance: recording the screen on macOS and Windows shows no island; toggle default is ON.

**FR-18** On Linux, where no reliable capture-exclusion API exists, the system MUST implement the
documented behavior chosen in OQ-5 and MUST NOT claim invisibility it cannot deliver.
- Acceptance: Linux behavior matches the documented decision and is surfaced to the user.

## 6. Design Considerations

- **Authoritative numbers:** the mockup's anatomy tables and `island.settings.json` are the source of
  truth. `tasks/dynamic-island-ui-research.md` is the evidence base. Port the mockup's `notchPath()`
  generator, rAF damped-spring integrator, `--di-wall` content rule, and Model B list logic; do not
  reinvent them.
- **Reuse:** island expanded content shares the card's content anatomy and the 27 `--s-*` overrides
  (`src/styles/overlay.css`). Whether to reuse `NotificationCard.tsx` or build a new component is an
  architecture-lane decision (see cross-references), not a PRD requirement.
- **Type pairing:** SF Pro for UI, SF Mono for sender / timers / ids / percentages (existing convention).
- **Reduced motion:** honor OS reduced-motion via the 1000/100 spring config.

---

## 7. Technical Considerations

- **Transport unchanged:** reuse HTTP `:9868` + WS `:9869` + `NotificationManager` event flow. No new
  transport (non-goal). The presentation field rides the existing schema.
- **Three-file type pattern:** the presentation field follows the existing enum mirroring across
  `cli/src/types.rs`, `src-tauri/src/notification/types.rs`, `src/types/notification.ts`.
- **New window:** the island is a distinct top-center, notch-anchored, capture-excluded window alongside
  the existing top-right panel (`src-tauri/src/overlay/panel.rs`). Single-window vs dedicated-window is
  an architecture decision; PRD requires only that the top-right card is undisturbed.
- **Two early platform gates (must precede dependent work):** (1) Tauri access path to NSScreen
  `auxiliaryTopLeftArea` / `auxiliaryTopRightArea` for notch width (OQ-3); (2) whether
  `set_content_protected(true)` applies to the `tauri-nspanel` window type (OQ-4).
- **Animation dependency:** hand-rolled rAF spring (already in the mockup) vs the `motion` library is an
  architecture-lane call; either way visual verification is Playwright-based because layout animation
  does not run in jsdom.
- **Regression surface (syncfu, NOT the 6 Meetily KPIs):** top-right overlay behavior, HTTP/WS API
  compatibility, CLI flag compatibility, history/SQLite.

---

## 8. Non-Goals (inversion pass)

Adjacent things this feature could plausibly do but explicitly WILL NOT:

- **Not replacing the top-right card.** Both presentations coexist; the card is untouched.
- **Not a menu-bar / HUD / media-controller / dashboard product.** This is a notification presentation,
  not a boring.notch-style always-present system dashboard.
- **No new transport.** No new ports, no new server; reuse HTTP/WS + `NotificationManager`.
- **No per-notification geometry.** Senders never set width, height, position, mode, or opacity. Only the
  27 style overrides are per-notification.
- **Overflow Model A (badge + cycle) is REJECTED.** Not built; guarded against reintroduction (FR-13).
- **Overflow Model C (stack-under) is REJECTED.** The named anti-pattern no mature app ships; not built;
  guarded (FR-13).
- **No Linux capture-exclusion guarantee.** Linux has no reliable API; only a documented behavior ships
  (FR-18). The island will not pretend to be invisible on Linux.
- **No settings sync across machines.** Persistent settings are local to the app install for this
  release.
- **No redesign of shape/motion/overflow.** The mockup's numbers are locked (D3/D5); implementation ports
  them.

---

## 9. Success Metrics

- Functional parity: 100% of the FR-14 behavior matrix passes in island mode.
- Visual fidelity: island states match the mockup `shot-*` gallery within the agreed visual-regression
  tolerance.
- Capture exclusion: 0 island frames captured across the macOS and Windows recording tests (dedicated
  track).
- Zero regression: existing top-right card, HTTP/WS, CLI, and history test suites remain green.
- Wall-inset invariant: 0 content-vs-shape collisions across the full geometry range.

**Pre-drafting thinking passes (recorded per skill):**
- **Primary job (JTBD):** a developer running long AI-agent tasks wants ambient, glanceable status and
  safe approval prompts that never leak on a live screen share, without the notification stealing focus
  or window space.
- **Top unstated assumptions surfaced (socratic):** (1) that a single presentation field, not a broader
  "kind" taxonomy, is the right routing primitive (resolved: retire "kind", use "presentation");
  (2) that capture exclusion actually applies to the NSPanel window type used today (unresolved, OQ-4,
  material to scope); (3) that island and card can coexist without a routing conflict (unresolved, OQ-9,
  material to scope).
